item.title: Cell Production-History Traceability Tool
item.description:
Project type
Field-used manufacturing DX
Build period
About three weeks · direct build
Technology
Excel Power Query · VBA
Relationship keys
Cell S/N · J/R · material lot · process time
Search result
About 5–10 sec per cell · about 3 min for ten cells
Work result
About three days → about half a day including report · field handoff

Project background and objective

The NCM pilot line already had MES exports and Excel records for electrode, assembly, inspection, and formation processes. The missing function was a continuous cell-level path across those records.

item.title: Indy7 Digital Twin
item.description:
What an interviewer should confirm in 30 seconds

Item Scope
Project A 10-person automotive-factory training PoC connecting QR, vision, collaborative robots, PLC/SCADA, and a database
Problem Individual robot motion was not enough; product identity, completion state, inspection result, and loading history had to remain connected
What I led Overall planning of the project goal, process scenario, system structure, and cross-team integration order
Direct hands-on scope Indy7 control, command/state integration between stations, robot programs, and integrated-flow validation
Team boundary Detailed vision, PLC Ladder, and SCADA/database work belonged to teammates; the team lead owned the report, schedule, and final presentation
Verified output Physical flow from QR capture through body/window assembly, vision inspection, and good/defect routing
Later extension PC-HMI, Conty JSON, IndyDCP, MQTT, history services, and a read-only web twin were developed later as a separate public-code scope

How to read this table: I led the project problem framing and integration order. My direct implementation centered on Indy7 control and process integration, while detailed vision, Ladder, SCADA, and team-lead responsibilities remain separately attributed.
